domain_setting: A traveler moves between lodging, hotel services, reservations, airport procedures, and holiday activities, using a compact luggage-and-journey world that spans city hotels, countryside stays, and flights.
recurring_scale_anchors: Use a 304x192 stage and keep the key subject inside x=24..280 and y=18..174.
Keep one consistent adult traveler silhouette and one compact rolling suitcase as scale cues; show limbs as solid tapered shapes or thick double-stroked forms, never thin stick lines.
Reuse the same warm hotel-front-desk materials, blue key cards, amber booking accents, and dark slate luggage across lodging and service scenes.
Airport scenes use a consistent passenger jet, boarding bridge, gate arch, runway, and glass terminal geometry.
Room scenes show beds, doors, windows, furniture, luggage, and services with clear differences at thumbnail size.
Do not place readable signs, letters, numerals, dates, prices, logos, passport text, room numbers, or route labels in artwork.

polysemy_resolution_table.accommodation: Lodging for a traveler, illustrated with places to stay rather than a social arrangement.
polysemy_resolution_table.reception: The hotel's guest reception/front desk, following its rooms-and-services group, not accepting something or a social event.
polysemy_resolution_table.safe: A hotel room that feels secure, shown with a working door lock and traveler at ease; not a strongbox.
polysemy_resolution_table.check in: The verb/action of arriving at a hotel and registering at the desk.
polysemy_resolution_table.check-in: The hotel arrival/registration checkpoint or counter as a service point, distinct from the action phrase.
polysemy_resolution_table.check out: The action of leaving a hotel and returning its key card at the desk.
polysemy_resolution_table.check-out: The hotel departure/checkout point and its returned key card, distinct from the action phrase.
polysemy_resolution_table.flight: Passenger airplane travel through the air, selected by the airports group, not a bird's flight.
polysemy_resolution_table.room: A hotel guest room, shown with its own bed, door, and window, not a generic room in a house.
polysemy_resolution_table.vacation: A period of leisure travel away from home, selected by the travel activities group, not only time off work.
polysemy_resolution_table.one-way: Travel in one direction without a return leg, shown as a single journey route.
polysemy_resolution_table.one-way ticket: A physical travel ticket for a single outward journey, not the abstract route direction.
polysemy_resolution_table.round-trip: A journey with an outward leg and a return leg to the starting point.
polysemy_resolution_table.round-trip ticket: A physical ticket that represents both outward and return travel legs.
polysemy_resolution_table.be delayed: The passenger's experience of waiting because departure is postponed.
polysemy_resolution_table.delayed: The postponed departure status of a plane, shown as the aircraft held at the terminal/runway.
polysemy_resolution_table.boarding pass: A travel document used to board an aircraft, shown without lettering, codes, or digits.
polysemy_resolution_table.key card: A flat electronic hotel room access card, distinct from a metal key.
polysemy_resolution_table.all-inclusive: A holiday stay whose lodging, meals, and activities are bundled together.
polysemy_resolution_table.bed and breakfast: A small lodging with a guest bed and a morning meal, not merely a bedroom or cafe.
polysemy_resolution_table.cabin: A simple rustic wooden dwelling, often isolated in woodland.
polysemy_resolution_table.chalet: A mountain holiday house with a wide sloping roof and alpine setting.
polysemy_resolution_table.motel: A roadside lodging with parking immediately beside guest-room doors.
polysemy_resolution_table.hostel: Budget lodging with shared bunks and communal space, not a private hotel room.
polysemy_resolution_table.dorm: A shared sleeping room with multiple beds for students or travelers, not a whole hostel building.
polysemy_resolution_table.villa: A private holiday house in a warm southern European setting, not a resort hotel.
polysemy_resolution_table.rent a cottage: A traveler obtains temporary use of a small cottage, shown with a key handover and bag at the door.
polysemy_resolution_table.room service: Hotel staff brings a meal on a covered tray into a guest room.
polysemy_resolution_table.laundry service: Hotel collection and return of guests' washed, folded, or pressed clothing.
polysemy_resolution_table.no vacancies: Every guest room is occupied, communicated with full room windows and unavailable-status markers without words.
polysemy_resolution_table.vacancies: Open guest rooms are available, communicated with visible unoccupied beds and available-status markers without words.
polysemy_resolution_table.cruise: A leisure journey aboard a passenger ship, not a fast crossing ferry.
polysemy_resolution_table.excursion: A short organized outing to a nearby destination, often with a small group.
polysemy_resolution_table.go on an excursion: A group actively leaves on a short guided outing; distinguish from the excursion destination itself.
polysemy_resolution_table.go sightseeing: A traveler visits and looks at notable local landmarks.
polysemy_resolution_table.sightseeing: The activity of viewing landmarks, with attention on the places being observed.
polysemy_resolution_table.guidebook: A printed travel reference book with place illustrations, not a phrasebook.
polysemy_resolution_table.phrasebook: A small book of useful spoken phrases represented with speech bubbles and language icons but no writing.
polysemy_resolution_table.passport: A physical identity and travel document used for crossing borders, with no readable text or numbers.
polysemy_resolution_table.passport control: An airport border checkpoint where an officer checks travelers' passports before passage.
polysemy_resolution_table.scales: A physical luggage-weighing device when encountered in a hotel or airport context.

sibling_contrasts.lodging_types: Accommodation is the broad category; hotel is a larger serviced building; motel has rooms opening directly to parking; hostel has shared bunks; dorm is one shared sleeping room; bed and breakfast is a small hosted home with breakfast; guesthouse is a small staffed lodging; cabin is rustic woodland woodwork; chalet is alpine; villa is a warm-climate private house; cottage is a small rentable holiday home; apartment is a self-contained multi-unit residence.
sibling_contrasts.hotel_rooms: Single room has one bed; double room has one shared double bed; twin beds are two separate matching beds; en-suite bathroom connects directly to the guest room; room with a view frames a distinctive landscape; safe emphasizes secure access rather than a storage box.
sibling_contrasts.hotel_services: Front desk/reception are the guest-facing counter; key card is the room-access item; room service brings a meal; laundry service returns cleaned clothing; check-in concerns arrival; check-out concerns departure; vacancies/no vacancies use opposite availability states.
sibling_contrasts.booking_and_tickets: Make a reservation and reservation differ as action versus confirmed booking; book a vacation focuses on arranging the whole trip; one-way and round-trip show route shapes; one-way ticket and round-trip ticket show the physical ticket documents; rental car centers on a borrowed car; travel insurance centers on protection against trip problems.
sibling_contrasts.airport_actions: Board a plane shows passengers entering it; flight shows an airborne plane; land at the airport shows touchdown; be delayed shows a waiting passenger; delayed shows an aircraft held from departure; departure gate is the terminal passage to the aircraft; passport control is the border checkpoint.
sibling_contrasts.travel_activities: Cruise/go on a cruise use ship travel; vacation/go on a vacation separate the holiday from the act of leaving; excursion/go on an excursion separate the short outing from setting out; sightseeing/go sightseeing separate the activity from a traveler actively visiting landmarks; walking vacation is a multi-day journey on foot.

art_direction: Make travel scenes warm and editorial, with paper and linen surfaces, restrained slate-blue luggage, amber service cues, soft garden sage, and clear architectural silhouettes. Choose one unmistakable moment per card and keep all text, letters, digits, labels, and symbols out of the art. Keep travelers volumetric and expressive with solid tapered limbs, simple clothing shapes, and no stick figures.
